## 1. Learning objectives
After this lesson you can:
- write a `while (true)` menu loop that shows choices, reads one, acts, and repeats;
- split the work into one small method per menu choice;
- catch the end of the input with `try` / `catch` so the program stops politely;
- write a test that "types" a whole session and checks the screen output;
- finish **Milestone M2** and demo an interactive Inventory & Sales app.

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- A **menu loop** is the heart of every console app: *show the choices, read one, do it, go back to the top.*
  The loop only ends when the person chooses **Quit** (`return` leaves the method).
- **One method per choice** (`addProduct`, `receiveStock`, `recordSale`, `showReport`) keeps each part small.
  The loop only decides *which* method to call. This is called **separation of concerns**.
- **Check, then act.** Before a sale we check the product exists and there is enough stock, and print a friendly
  message if not. The `Inventory` also refuses bad requests on its own (it returns `false` / `-1`), so the data
  can never be damaged even if the menu has a bug.
- **try / catch** (full story in lesson 16): `try { ... } catch (NoSuchElementException e) { ... }` means "run this;
  if the Scanner runs out of input and throws that exception, jump to the catch block". We use it so that pressing
  Ctrl+D (end of input) or a test that ran out of lines ends the program with `Input ended. Goodbye.` instead of a crash.
- **Testing a conversation.** Because `Menu.run(in, out, inventory)` takes the `Scanner` and `PrintStream` as
  parameters, a test can pass `new Scanner("3\nrice 25kg\n2\n5\n")` (the keystrokes) and read back everything that was
  printed. No keyboard, always the same result.
- **Money is still `int` centavos.** Prices are limited to PHP 10,000.00 and sale quantities to 100 at a time, so the
  arithmetic can never overflow an `int`. (Week 5 introduces `BigDecimal`.)

## 3. Runnable sample code
`examples/MenuDemo.java` — a tiny menu (a counter) driven by a pretend keyboard. Run from the repo root:
```
java lessons/08-console-menu/examples/MenuDemo.java
```
The loop at its core:
```java
boolean running = true;
while (running) {
    // print the menu, read a line
    if (line.equals("1")) { counter++; }
    else if (line.equals("3")) { running = false; }
    else { System.out.println("Please choose 1, 2 or 3."); }
}
```

5. **TODO 4 — `recordSale`**: ask for the name; unknown → message and `return`; ask the quantity; if it is more than

## 5. Practical exercises
In `exercises/` (`Exercises08.java`, tests in `Exercises08Test.java`):
1. `numberedMenu(options)` — `{"Add", "Sell"}` becomes `"1. Add\n2. Sell"`.
2. `optionAt(options, choice)` — the option text, or `"Invalid choice"` outside `1..options.length`.
3. `isQuitCommand(text)` — `q`, `quit` or `exit`, any capitals, spaces ignored.

*Stretch:* add a menu choice 5 "Low-stock list" (and move Quit to 6). Update `menuText`, `run` and the tests.

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Menu tests fail with a message mismatch | A prompt or message differs by one character | Copy the text from the TODO comments exactly |
| The menu never ends | Choice 5 does not `return` | Print `Goodbye.` then `return;` |
| `Input ended. Goodbye.` appears in a test | The test did not type enough lines (or forgot `5`) | Add the missing answers and the final `5` |
| Stack trace `NoSuchElementException: No line found` | No `catch` around the loop | Add the `catch (NoSuchElementException e)` block |
| Sale succeeds with more than the stock | Skipped the "not enough stock" check | Compare with `inventory.quantityOf(stored)` before selling |
| Product is added twice with different capitals | Skipped `inventory.find(name)` | `find` ignores capitals and extra spaces; check it first |
| Prices show wrong by 100x | Typed centavos instead of pesos | Type `35` or `35.00` for PHP 35.00 |
